title: Check: taints and tolerations
description: Five questions on keeping Pods off nodes.

questions.prompt: What is the relationship between a taint and a toleration?

options.text: A taint attracts Pods; a toleration repels them
A taint on a node repels Pods; a toleration on a Pod lets it ignore that taint

questions.explanation: Taints are node-side and repel. Tolerations are Pod-side and grant an exception - they do not attract.

questions.prompt: Which taint effect evicts Pods that are already running?
questions.explanation: NoSchedule only blocks new placement. NoExecute also evicts Pods that do not tolerate it.

questions.prompt: Write the command that taints node worker-2 so ordinary Pods will not schedule there, using key=gpu value=true.
questions.explanation: Append a minus - `gpu=true:NoSchedule-` - to remove it.

questions.prompt: Why does a Pod usually not schedule onto a control plane node?

options.text: Control plane nodes have no CPU left

questions.explanation: That taint is why a two-node cluster can look half empty while a Pod sits Pending.

questions.prompt: A toleration with `operator: Exists` and no value means what?

options.text: It tolerates any value for that key
It tolerates only an empty value

questions.explanation: Exists ignores the value. Omitting the key as well tolerates every taint - which is how some system DaemonSets run everywhere.
